2607.02432.title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach
2607.02432.paper_summary: Scalable and reliable grading of command-line examinations remains a challenge in computing education, where rising enrolments make manual marking difficult and rule-based autograders cannot handle partial credit, equivalent solutions, or syntactic variation. This paper evaluates whether four frontier Large Language Models (GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM) can approximate expert judgment when grading short Linux/bash command responses. The study adopts a four-level cognitive taxonomy that combines cognitive complexity and operational impact, ranging from information retrieval (L1) and basic file manipulation (L2) to structural operations (L3) and advanced system management (L4). The models were tested with two prompt variants, a minimal baseline and a rubric-enhanced version, on 1200 real responses from second-year Computer Engineering students independently graded by three expert instructors. Gemini~3.0 Pro with rubric-guided prompting achieved the highest human-AI agreement (ICC(3,1) = 0.888, MAE = 0.10, Bland-Altman bias = -0.014). Agreement declined consistently as taxonomy level increased, with the largest discrepancies at higher levels. Across all models, rubric quality had a larger effect than provider choice, with structured prompts consistently improving agreement. These results show that question complexity is a reliable predictor of the difficulty LLMs face in grading accurately, and they establish a principled, taxonomy-based framework for determining which questions are suitable for AI-assisted grading and which require human review, while also providing a transferable evaluation protocol and prompt templates.
2607.02432.paper_summary_zh: 可擴展且可靠的命令列考試評分在計算機教育中仍然是一個挑戰，隨著入學人數的上升，手動評分變得困難，而基於規則的自動評分工具無法處理部分得分、等價解決方案或語法變異。本文評估四種前沿大型語言模型（GPT、Claude Opus、Gemini 和 GLM）在評分短的 Linux/bash 命令回應時是否能夠接近專家判斷。該研究採用一種四級認知分類法，結合了認知複雜性和操作影響，範圍從信息檢索（L1）和基本文件操作（L2）到結構操作（L3）和高級系統管理（L4）。這些模型在 1200 個來自二年級計算機工程學生的真實回應上進行了測試，這些回應由三位專家教師獨立評分，使用了兩種提示變體：一個最小基線和一個增強的評分標準版本。使用評分標準引導提示的 Gemini~3.0 Pro 達到了最高的人類與 AI 一致性（ICC(3,1) = 0.888，MAE = 0.10，Bland-Altman 偏差 = -0.014）。隨著分類法級別的提高，一致性穩定下降，在較高級別上出現了最大的差異。在所有模型中，評分標準的質量對結果的影響大於提供者的選擇，結構化提示始終改善了一致性。這些結果顯示問題的複雜性是預測 LLM 在準確評分時面臨困難的可靠指標，並建立了一個原則性的、基於分類法的框架，以確定哪些問題適合 AI 協助評分，哪些需要人類審查，同時還提供了一個可轉移的評估協議和提示模板。
